title: Settling Fuel at the End of a Car Rental
content:
The fuel arrangement is the rate class's own: a full-to-full class expects the vehicle back with a full
tank, a same-to-same class expects it back at the level it left with, and a prepaid class sells the tank in
advance at the class's own price per gallon. Every one of the Car Rental Rate Classes names one of the
three.

## When a fuel settlement may be raised

A fuel settlement is raised only while the rental record stands at picked up or returned. The rental record
decides this: no settlement is raised against a rental standing at merely booked, confirmed, cancelled, a
no-show or closed.

## Where the vehicle comes back short

Where a full-to-full or same-to-same vehicle comes back short, the missing fuel is charged at the class's
price per gallon and the class's refuelling service charge is added once.

The refuelling service charge is never charged twice on one rental, and never where the shortfall is less
than a quarter of a gallon. The minimum shortfall at which it may be charged at all is therefore 0.25 of a
gallon.

| Shortfall at return, in gallons | At or above the minimum of 0.25 | Refuelling service charge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1 | no | none |
| 0.25 | yes | charged once |
| 3.4 | yes | charged once |
| 3.4, on a rental that already carries the charge | yes | not charged a second time |

## Where a prepaid tank comes back with fuel in it

Where a prepaid class vehicle comes back with fuel still in it, nothing is returned, because the tank was
sold and not lent.

## The renter who refuels for themselves

A renter who refuels at a filling station and keeps the receipt is charged nothing at all, whatever the
class, provided the tank meets the class's expectation.
